outcomes.finding: On the representative public-source acquisition task, elapsed waiting/serialization was a demonstrated bottleneck: bounded 4-worker acquisition preserved 8/8 success while reducing elapsed time from 3136.4 ms to 785.3 ms (3.994x).

The first broad P1 capture path stalled on slow sources. The recovery changed the procedure to per-item bounded execution/failure isolation, documented it in a durable runbook, and the comparable replay completed with terminal results for all 8 sampled sources.

Net utility was measured instead of assumed. For this acquisition path, the bounded-parallel implementation had positive net utility (same 8/8 success, about 3.994x lower elapsed wall time). This supports measurement-before-default, not a universal claim about all tools.

A stale-looking Claude subscription-auth condition was observed against current non-secret auth metadata, but changing an authentication boundary was intentionally not performed through the blocked tool path. The candidate rule is not adopted or removed.

A durable acquisition runbook now exists and one comparable replay passed. This is insufficient to establish repeatability across a fresh independent executor/session, so the learning remains open for a second real continuation.
